evidence.claim: The Speed Tax: To search 10M vectors at sub-10ms speed, you may need 64GB+ of dedicated RAM.

evidence.claim: Vector databases have p99 latency and concurrent QPS as key performance metrics
evidence.quote: Latency p99 (99th percentile, measuring the slowest 1% of queries) matters more than median. Slow tail queries degrade user experience more than good medians improve it. A system with 10ms median and 500ms p99 feels slower than 20ms median and 50ms p99.

evidence.claim: Concurrent throughput (QPS) is a key performance metric for vector databases
evidence.quote: Concurrent throughput (QPS) shows behavior under actual load. A database handling 100 simultaneous queries at 30ms beats one that does 1 query at 10ms but drops to 200ms under load. Single-query benchmarks lie about production performance.

evidence.claim: pgvector + pgvectorscale stores vectors in PostgreSQL with under 100M vectors, requiring less storage than purpose-built databases
evidence.quote: pgvector + pgvectorscale: PostgreSQL users with under 100M vectors, plus iterative index scans for better filtered search.

evidence.claim: Purpose-built databases like Pinecone, Milvus, Qdrant, and Weaviate handle billions of vectors with lower storage costs than extensions
evidence.quote: Pinecone, Milvus, Qdrant, and Weaviate use vector-optimized storage engines, query planners, and index structures. They implement HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World), a graph-based algorithm that searches vectors by navigating through multiple layers from coarse to fine approximations. This handles billions of vectors well because algorithm complexity grows logarithmically, not linearly, regardless of vector dimensionality.

evidence.claim: Quantization reduces memory costs with minimal recall impact, cutting memory by 75% when reducing 32-bit floats to 8-bit integers
evidence.quote: Quantization (compressing vectors by using fewer bits per dimension, like reducing 32-bit floats to 8-bit integers) reduces memory costs with minimal recall impact. Reducing 32-bit floats to 8-bit integers cuts memory 75% while maintaining high accuracy.

evidence.claim: Write-heavy patterns like agent memory workloads require different recovery mechanisms than traditional RAG
evidence.quote: If your evaluation weights read latency alone, you'll pick the wrong database for anything with iterative writes.

evidence.quote: Semantic search is super-efficient, fast, and great for providing direct answers closely related to the user query.

evidence.claim: Semantic search is lightweight, scalable, and cost-efficient.
evidence.quote: Because it operates only on vector embeddings and retrieval algorithms, it’s lightweight, scalable, and cost-efficient.

evidence.quote: Costly if you want to handle massive datasets: Creating and updating vector embeddings for large datasets demands increasing amounts of resources, which can be expensive.
